cases.statement: One accession number (A0042) in PMID 22134107; Table I gives 1 family (1 allele), citing reference [50]. A0042 is also listed in the c.1498delG (p.Asp500ThrfsX29) row.

people.label: A0042
people.zygosity_or_genotype: heterozygous for this variant, implied compound heterozygous (1 allele; A0042 also listed under c.1498delG)
people.other_allele: c.1498delG (p.Asp500ThrfsX29), listed under the same accession number
people.key_phenotypes: LAD-I type of the table row: LAD-I^o (CD18 present at < 5% of normal expression, per the table legend); no clinical features reported per person

quotes.quote: In this nomenclature the superscript symbol indicates whether the protein is present at < 5% of normal expression (^o), diminished in expression (^−), i.e. between 5% and 20% of normal expression, or normally present but nonfunctional (^+)

This information is based on immune reactivity of the patients’ leukocytes with monoclonal antibodies analyzed by flow cytometry and sometimes on similar analyses of COS cells cotransfected with mutant CD18 molecules and wild-type CD11 molecules.

phenotype_specificity.statement: PMID 22134107 gives no person-level clinical features or exclusion of other causes; it describes the disease only in general terms.

quotes.quote: Characteristic features are delayed separation of the umbilical cord and strong leukocytosis, especially neutrophilia, during periods of infection.
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].

de_novo.statement: Not tested in PMID 22134107. The cited source [50] has a title that mentions "de novo mutations"; its content was not read here, and which variant or person it refers to is not stated in this paper.

quotes.quote: Two novel frame shift, recurrent and de novo mutations in the ITGB2 (CD18) gene causing leukocyte adhesion deficiency in a highly inbred North African population

in_trans.statement: A0042 is listed under both c.1920delG (1 family, 1 allele) and c.1498delG. Phase was not shown in this paper; no parental testing is reported.

functional.statement: Table I gives LAD-I^o (CD18 present at < 5% of normal expression, per the table legend). Per the legend, this class is based on flow cytometry of the patients' leukocytes and sometimes on COS-cell co-transfection; which material was used for this variant is not stated, and no numeric results or controls are given.

quotes.quote: In this nomenclature the superscript symbol indicates whether the protein is present at < 5% of normal expression (^o), diminished in expression (^−), i.e. between 5% and 20% of normal expression, or normally present but nonfunctional (^+)

This information is based on immune reactivity of the patients’ leukocytes with monoclonal antibodies analyzed by flow cytometry and sometimes on similar analyses of COS cells cotransfected with mutant CD18 molecules and wild-type CD11 molecules.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Batch HGVS: single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift, p.(Lys641ArgfsTer17), which agrees with the paper's p.Lys641ArgfsX17. The paper describes the disease as caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (the β2 integrin subunit).

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.

authors_classification.statement: The variant is listed in Table I, which the authors title as mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2; no per-variant classification or ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: TABLE I: Mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2

concerns: PMID 22134107 is a mutation-update table (Table I) without case descriptions: people are identified only by database accession numbers, and sex, age and clinical features are not given per person.

In Table I the LAD-I type and the families (alleles) count belong to the table row (the variant), not to one accession number; for an accession number listed with a second variant, the expression class reflects the person's genotype, not this allele alone.
A0042 carries a second listed variant, c.1498delG (candidate G-lad1-025 in this batch, same identity LAD1-ID0357).

The cited source [50] (Fathallah et al. 2001) is titled as reporting recurrent and de novo frameshift mutations in a highly inbred North African population; it was not available to this dossier, so any de novo claim is unverified here.
notes_for_panel: Same person as the c.1498delG carrier A0042 in G-lad1-025.
